info.title: Gingr API
info.description:
Welcome to the **Gingr API** — a RESTful JSON:API-compliant interface for integrating with Gingr, the leading pet-care business management platform.

## Authentication

All requests require an API key passed in the `X-Api-Key` header. Keys are scoped to a specific organization and can be generated from the Gingr admin dashboard under **Settings → Integrations → API Keys**.

## Subdomain Header

Every request must also include a `subdomain` header identifying which Gingr account you are operating on. This value is the subdomain portion of your Gingr URL (e.g., `mykennel` for `mykennel.gingrapp.com`).

## Response Format

The API follows the [JSON:API v1.0](https://jsonapi.org/) specification. All requests must include:

```
Accept: application/vnd.api+json
```

POST/PUT/PATCH requests that include a body must also include:

```
Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json
```

Paginated list responses include a `meta` object with `currentPage`, `lastPage`, `perPage`, and `total`, as well as a `links` object with `first`, `last`, `prev`, and `next` cursor URLs.

## Error Handling

| HTTP Status | Meaning |
|-------------|---------|
| 200 | Success |
| 201 | Resource created |
| 400 | Bad request / business logic error |
| 401 | Unauthorized — invalid or missing API key |
| 403 | Forbidden — valid key but insufficient permissions |
| 404 | Resource not found |
| 422 | Validation error — see `errors` array in response |
| 500 | Internal server error |

Validation errors (`422`) are returned as a JSON:API `errors` array where each item contains a `title` and a `detail` describing the offending field.

## Rate Limiting

API requests are subject to rate limiting. Exceeding the limit returns a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Contact Gingr support to discuss higher rate limits for high-volume integrations.

tags.name: Config
tags.description:
The **Config** group exposes read and write endpoints for all organization-level configuration data in Gingr. This includes the lookup tables and settings that everything else depends on — species, breeds, booking types, service options, feeding options, immunization types, forms, locations, hours of operation, tax rates, areas, disabled dates, and more.

Typically you will call these endpoints once at startup (or on a periodic refresh) to build local caches that your integration can reference when creating bookings, parents, and pets. Most config data changes infrequently and is safe to cache for hours or even days.

Key things to know:

- **Booking Types** define the kinds of services a location offers (e.g., Boarding, Daycare, Grooming). A booking must reference a valid booking type for the target location.
- **Service Options** are add-ons that can be attached to a booking (e.g., extra walks, nail trim). Each service option belongs to a booking type.
- **Forms** are questionnaires associated with bookings or animals. Form answers are collected during the pre-check process.
- **Areas / Runs** represent physical kennel spaces. Lodging availability and capacity constraints live here.
- **Tax Rates** define the tax rules applied when invoicing. Whether tax is applied to a booking depends on organization settings.
- **Disabled Dates** let you know when a location is closed so you can avoid booking on those days.

tags.name: Parents
tags.description:
The **Parents** group covers everything related to the pet owner — referred to as a **Parent** in Gingr. A Parent is the primary account holder who owns one or more animals and makes bookings.

Use this group to:

- **Create** new parents during the intake flow (e.g., an online booking portal).
- **Update** parent profile data such as contact info, address, and custom fields.
- **Search / list** parents by name, email, phone, and other filters.
- **Manage memberships** — enroll or cancel a parent's membership plan.
- **Manage cards on file** — retrieve saved payment methods so you can pre-fill checkout forms.
- **Handle agreements** — check which digital waivers a parent still needs to sign and mark them as signed.

Important considerations:

- `email` and `cellPhone` are unique per organization. Attempting to create a duplicate will return a `422` validation error.
- `allowOnlineLogin` controls whether the parent can log in to the Gingr consumer portal. This defaults to `false` for API-created parents unless explicitly set.
- Custom fields (configured per organization) can be passed in the `customFields` object. Field keys vary by organization — use the Config `/v1/config` endpoint or contact support to get the key names for a specific subdomain.

tags.name: Bookings
tags.description:
The **Bookings** group is the core of the Gingr API. A **Booking** (also called a Reservation internally) represents a scheduled service for one or more animals at a specific location and time.

The typical booking lifecycle is:

1. **Validate** — Call the validation endpoints to check availability and confirm there are no conflicts before committing.
2. **Create** — Submit the booking with the required fields. The response includes the new booking ID.
3. **Pre-check** — If the organization requires a pre-check, retrieve the pre-check form (`GET /v1/bookings/{id}/precheck-form`) and submit answers (`POST /v1/bookings/{id}/precheck`).
4. **Accept / Confirm** — Some organizations require staff to manually confirm bookings. Use the accept endpoint when `manualConfirm` is enabled.
5. **Checkout** — When the service is complete, submit payment via the checkout endpoint.
6. **Cancel** — If needed, cancel the booking and optionally apply a cancellation fee.

Key concepts:

- **`manualConfirm`** — When this flag is `true` on a booking type, new bookings land in a "pending" state and must be explicitly accepted by staff before they are considered confirmed. If `false`, bookings are auto-confirmed.
- **Overrides** — The `overrides` object in the create/update requests lets you bypass certain business rule validations (e.g., overbooking a run, scheduling outside business hours). Overrides require elevated API permissions and should be used sparingly.
- **Services** — A booking can have one or more services attached (e.g., the base boarding service plus grooming add-ons). Services carry their own pricing and scheduling.
- **Lodging** — For overnight boarding, the booking is assigned to a specific run/kennel. The available lodgings endpoint returns which runs are open for the requested dates.
- **Pre-check** — A digital check-in form that collects health, feeding, and care instructions for the animal's stay. Whether pre-check is required depends on organization settings.
- **Standing Bookings** — Recurring bookings on a fixed schedule (e.g., every Monday for daycare). Changes to a standing booking can apply to the single instance or all future occurrences.

tags.name: Pets
tags.description:
The **Pets** group manages **Animals** — the pets that belong to a Parent. In Gingr, the internal model is called `Animal` but the API surfaces it as `Pet` for clarity.

Use this group to:

- **List** all pets for a parent or search across the organization.
- **Create** a new pet and associate it with an existing parent.
- **Update** pet profile data including breed, weight, birthdate, and special notes.
- **Manage immunizations** — attach vaccination records required before the animal can be booked.
- **Manage medications** — record medications the animal is currently taking so staff are informed during the stay.
- **Retrieve feeding instructions** — feeding details attached to the pet for use during overnight stays.

Key things to know:

- A pet must belong to a **Parent** — you cannot create a pet without a valid `parentId`.
- **Species** and **Breed** must reference valid IDs from the Config endpoints (`/v1/species`, `/v1/breeds`).
- **Immunization requirements** vary by organization and booking type. Check the Config immunization endpoints to know which vaccines are required for a given booking.
- A pet can have a **temperament** flag that may affect which runs or services are available for booking.

tags.name: Payments
tags.description:
The **Payments** group covers payment processing, invoice management, and deposit handling for bookings and retail transactions.

Use this group to:

- **Retrieve invoices** for a parent or booking.
- **Process payments** against an open invoice using a saved card on file or a new payment token.
- **Manage deposits** — collect or refund deposit amounts tied to a booking.
- **Handle store credit** — apply store credit balances toward an invoice.
- **Manage Card Vault (CVF) settings** — configure how cards are captured and stored for a parent.

Important considerations:

- Payments are processed through the payment gateway configured for the organization. The API does not accept raw card numbers — always use a payment token or a saved `paymentMethodId`.
- Refunds require a `refundReasonId` from the Config refund reasons endpoint.
- Deposit rules (amount, timing, refundability) are controlled by organization settings and booking type configuration.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description:
The **Invoices** group provides detailed access to Gingr's invoicing system. Invoices are generated automatically when a booking is created or when retail items are added to a parent's account.

Use this group to retrieve invoice line items, apply discounts, add open items, and query payment history. For processing actual payments against an invoice, see the **Payments** group.

Invoice statuses you may encounter:

- **Estimate** — Pre-service invoice that has not yet been finalized.
- **Open** — Invoice is finalized and awaiting payment.
- **Paid** — Invoice has been fully settled.
- **Void** — Invoice has been cancelled.

tags.name: Card On File
tags.description:
The **Card On File** group manages saved payment methods for a parent. Gingr stores tokenized card details through its payment gateway integration — raw card numbers are never stored or transmitted through the API.

Use this group to:

- **List** saved cards for a parent.
- **Set a default** card to use for auto-billing and deposits.
- **Delete** a card that is no longer needed.
- **Initiate card capture** flows for parents who need to add a new card.

Cards on file are required for certain features such as automatic deposits, membership auto-billing, and one-click checkout.

tags.name: Group Classes
tags.description:
The **Group Classes** group manages enrollment in structured group training and activity sessions. Unlike individual bookings, group classes have a fixed schedule, a capacity limit, and a roster of enrolled animals.

Use this group to list available class sessions, check capacity, enroll an animal, and retrieve class rosters. Pricing for group classes is set at the class-type level in the Config group.

tags.name: Precheck
tags.description:
The **Precheck** group handles the digital pre-check-in process for bookings. A pre-check collects animal care instructions — feeding, medications, behavioral notes, and custom form answers — before the animal arrives for its stay.

Whether pre-check is required depends on the organization's settings and the booking type. When required, a booking cannot be fully confirmed until a pre-check has been submitted.

Use this group to retrieve the pre-check form definition for a booking and to submit completed form answers.

tags.name: Upload
tags.description:
The **Upload** group provides endpoints for attaching files to parent and pet records. Supported file types include images (profile photos) and documents (vaccination certificates, signed waivers, etc.).

Uploaded files are stored in Gingr's file storage and associated with the relevant parent or pet record. File size and type restrictions apply — see individual endpoint documentation for limits.
